title: Safe agent config for both tools
goal: Replace an over-permissive starter config with guardrails: tests and lint run without prompts, network access is blocked, secrets are unreadable, and writes stay inside the repo. Do it for Claude Code (.claude/settings.json) and Codex CLI (.codex/config.toml), editing the files by hand BEFORE launching any agent in the folder. A script checks the files, and you confirm the behavior afterwards.

starter_prompts.claude: Run `npm test` and `npm run lint`. Then try `curl https://example.com` and tell me exactly what happened. (Launch with `claude --permission-mode default`, only after node scripts/check-config.mjs passes.)
starter_prompts.codex: Run `npm test`. Then try to create ~/outside-repo.txt and tell me exactly what happened. (Launch with `codex --sandbox workspace-write --ask-for-approval on-request`, only after node scripts/check-config.mjs passes.)

solution_notes: Claude Code allows exactly two commands, `npm test` and `npm run lint`, by name. The starter's `Bash(*)` allowed every command, which is the same as turning the guardrails off. Narrow allow rules plus the sandbox give you quiet prompts without giving up control.

curl and wget are denied by rule, but a Bash deny rule only matches the command as written (`/usr/bin/curl` and `sh -c 'curl ...'` are not matched). That is why the sandbox is also on: it blocks network and out-of-repo writes at the OS level, whatever the command looks like. `allowUnsandboxedCommands: false` closes the retry-outside-the-sandbox escape hatch.

Codex needs no allow list for `npm test` or `npm run lint`. In the workspace-write sandbox they run inside it, so they never prompt. What Codex adds is the boundary: workspace-write confines writes to the repo, network access is off by default, and on-request approval asks only when something wants to leave the sandbox.

The starter's `danger-full-access` with `never` is the Codex equivalent of `--dangerously-skip-permissions`: no sandbox and no questions. Web search is a separate tool from command network access, so the solution disables it explicitly.
Both files are committed to the repo. Every engineer who clones it gets the same guardrails, and a personal override goes in `.claude/settings.local.json` or `~/.codex/config.toml`.
